dct:provenance:
- The configured discovery root was crawled through its public dataset API. All 1,294 current catalog records were inspected; two non-data media records (GIF and MP4) were excluded, yielding 1,292 data records.
- The two catalog records GLY_001488 and GLY_001490 resolve to the same verified direct file URL; they were consolidated into one FileObject so every non-empty top-level distribution contentUrl is unique.
- The complete current release 2.11.1 download set was retrieved (1,292 successful files; 46,825,155,474 bytes). The portal advertises 20 older versions in addition to 2.11.1 and exposes per-dataset history metadata. Those historical snapshots were discovered and assessed but were not downloaded or represented because their aggregate transfer would multiply an already 46.8 GB current-release crawl; this metadata describes the authoritative current-release catalog only.
- CSV and TSV record schemas use exact in-band header tokens observed in downloaded content. Datatypes were inferred conservatively from no more than four data rows after the header, with no more than five physical lines inspected per file.
- FASTA, N-Triples, RDF gzip, XML, PNG, SVG, and per-glycan visualization JSON files are represented as distributions but not as RecordSets because this run did not establish a safe row/field extraction model for those non-tabular or single-visualization-object formats.
- Archive members were enumerated without modifying their parent archives. The three image/visualization tar archives contain 58,962 PNG, 58,962 SVG, and 57,106 JSON rendering members. Those 175,030 visualization payloads are not independent record-bearing dataset files and remain represented by their three parent archive FileObjects; expanding them as individual distributions would falsely imply independent datasets. The two data ZIP archives contain 57 TSV plus one JSON member and 31 XML members, all 89 of which are represented as contained FileObjects.
- Top-level name and description are exact source text from the GlyGen dataset application title and its About response. License and conditionsOfAccess are sourced verbatim from the authoritative GlyGen license page. citeAs preserves the complete author list and bibliographic facts published in GlyGen's linked RIS citation file.

description: GlyGen (gly-glycobiology; gen-information), is an advanced glycoinformatics resource developed to facilitate discovery in basic and translational glycobiology research along with enhancing the integration of multidisciplinary information from diverse resources. GlyGen includes knowledge about molecular, biophysical and functional properties of glycans, genes, proteins and lipids organized in pathways and ontologies, plus a rapidly growing body of biological big data related to mutation and expression. GlyGen adopts an innovative user driven approach for implementing, prioritizing and knowledge disseminating tools to address the questions and needs of glycobiology community.
